items.title: Mrs. Arnold Metoyer Interview, 1960-10-19
items.q: you know something about him, Harry.

ctx.x: He must have loved his music as you say. He did. He really loved music.

And he'd never leave his horn nowhere else. Anywhere he was, his horn had to be with him. Sometimes people say, why don't you leave your horn if you're not going home now? Uh-uh. Take it with me. I can carry it. Stick it under his arm. Cover it on. Never, never, uh, lend nobody his mouthpiece. Never. But he, when, if he'd borrow a horn, he'd... He'd never use the, the mouthpiece, the horn. No. Take that one off and put his on. Put his. Well he could borrow a horn, John. He played, uh, you know something about…
Some trumpet players do that. They get a little hard callus. Well he never had that. He had a, he'd get a blister.
